I feel as though the hype generated from this game and the reviews before this are good enough testament to its quality however I do wanna voice my own thoughts. To start, would I say the game lives up to the hype/is it a good game/is it a good sequel to Hollow Knight? Yes, for the love of God yes, if a fan of the original Hollow Knight wanted more of it as well as a more challenging expirience, buy this game YESTERDAY. With my bias aside (as I have completed 100% of the original HK), I do belive that Silksong can stand on its own merit as a standalone game and doesn't require a nostalgia boost from the original in order to be good. I won't say anything else, but if you are a fan of the orginal Hollow Knight or are looking for an unforgetable Metroidvania-Soulslike expirience, then this is the game for you. I spent 20 Euros to buy it for myself and then 20 Euros to buy it for my friend and I still think I stole from Team Cherry.
P.S GETTING HYPED FOR SEA OF SORROW!!!

Hollow Knight is an extremely important game to me and ranks among my favorite games of all time. Needless to say Silksong had very high expectations to rise up to, and Team Cherry actually pulled it off.

Silksong is not a perfect game, but the high level of craftmanship across all categories of the game make it very close to one. There is not a single thing I can think of that Silksong does poorly. It's gameplay, exploration, atmospejre, music, narrative, surprises and secrets. All of it is at the very least good if not astounding. Hell its gameplay alone is one of the most expressive and fluid combat systems I've seen in a game.

Silksong can also be a very unforgiving game at points, and it's fair to dislike these aspects. However, I find it hard to say that the game would be better without its barbs. I suppose Silksong is polarizing in that way.

The rougher edges of Silksong can, and maybe will, alienate you, but I do really mean it when I say that this is one of the exciting and well-rounded gaming experiences I have ever played. 2025 has been an incredible year for video gaming, and yet Silksong still steals GOTY for me. I deeply recommend at least giving Silksong a chance to amaze you. It can be brutal and frustrating, but I promise the chance of seeing all that Pharloom can offer is 100% worth it.

Nevertheless, this is an incredible game which so much effort and love put in - you will regret not paying more to play it. :)

Definitely play hollow knight first. But if you loved hollow knight, there's like a 90% chance you'll love this. It's significantly harder and otherwise different in a lot of ways, but it builds on all the things that made hollow knight a masterpiece while also making a super unique identity for itself, and as a result it's a masterpiece in its own right.

There is absolutely no reason not to have difficulty settings in a video game. It is an accessibility issue and I am tired of hearing that it isn't. By making the game one difficulty (and a very hard difficulty at that) Team Cherry has made a game that is simply inaccessible to a large amount of players. They have made the game miserable simply for the purpose of being miserable and that is the single most braindead design decision I have ever seen games make. I paid for the damn game now let me play it.

Not to mention the areas and enemies just get repetitive and annoying after a while; it feels like they were pressured into making a sequel to hollow knight and did the bare minimum in doing so. I sure love getting lost in the third fucking forest area that is filled with even more borderline invisible traps this time. Needs more time in the oven, to put it lightly.

SIlksong takes everything previously established in Hollow Knight and builds on it in a way that feels both fresh and challenging. For fans of games that reward exploration and tenacity. This game remains surprising with just how much content is hidden away in this game. Highly recommend, especially for fans of Hollow Knight.

As a game designer I have to say that this game is a masterpiece. Map design is wonderful, the bosses are great and the abilities are fun to use. I truly can't think of any game design flaws in silksong except for some small ones like lack of control customization for controller and not getting to set custom bindings for using red tools. Also the fastest way to beat the game requires going trough the mist and that rng kind of ruins Any% speedruns of the game to me.

I really enjoy the game, but some of the design choices are legitimately irritating. For example:

1. The game starts you with 5 masks, yet something that becomes quickly apparent is that many enemies and nearly every boss deals 2 masks of damage every time they hit you. This makes the first mask feel significantly less impactful to earn, since Hornet goes from dying in 3 hits to still dying in 3 hits.
2. Grinding is practically a requirement if you want to regularly use your tools or the architect crest. In general it feels like this game is significantly more willing to waste your time than the original was.
3. The runbacks are unnecessarily long. For one boss in particular the runback is longer than the boss fight itself.

Team Cherry did an amazing job with the narrative and the environmental story telling was top notch. Many of the moments I find frustrating do a fantastic job at conveying the horrors of Pharloom. Nevertheless, from a gameplay perspective, they still feel bad.

A masterpiece in all aspects. Gameplay and movement feels smooth and snappy, combat is difficult but incredibly satisfying. The music and graphics are both works of art in their own right, and the story is amazing. One of my favorite games, and justifies the incredibly long development time.
If you enjoy metroidvanias, or just 2D games in general, I would highly recommend Silksong. I would also recommend playing the first Hollow Knight before this one, as both the story and difficultly feel like they pick up right where the first left off. With that in mind, be warned that this game is very difficult. If you get frustrated at bosses easily, this may not be the game for you.

My only suggestion is that this game is hard sometimes which is why playing the first game may make it easier. Overall, this is an amazing game!

The game is simply amazing. 10/10.

That being said, it can be a rough start if you’re coming straight from the original Hollow Knight. Hornet plays very differently. Her crests change how your attacks behave, and her silk skills are way more precise and limited compared to the Knight’s spells. You can’t just steamroll everything with magic anymore.

In exchange, Hornet feels fast and fluid. She’s got mobility and actual tools—different weapons with unique effects. They’re not overpowered, but if you use them right, they can absolutely turn a fight in your favor.

It’s also a longer game than the original, with more to explore and that same brutal, satisfying platforming that made me love the first one.

At first, I thought, “yeah… the original is better.”
But once it clicked? I honestly prefer Silksong.

My personal GOTY—you won’t regret it.

That said, if you don’t like difficult games, this isn’t for you. You will die… a lot…
Just now it’s Hornet serenading you with her needle instead of a tiny violin.

I'd say that this game is beautiful, that is if I were able to explore it. It's genuinely infuriating how freakishly strong every enemy is -- including random environmental enemies you find. Half the enemies deal double damage, all the bosses I've encountered do too, and one of the bosses I've encountered does _triple_ damage. Not to mention, _everything_ is punishing. Want to dash left after attacking right? Nope. You dash right because you didn't wait the extra 0.000001ms. Want to go visit a certain bench? Nope. Chances are it costs rosaries (which of course you no longer have as they're currently sitting in a boss arena anyway).

As Hollowknights successor this game has some ridiculously big shoes to fill and in my opinion manages to accomplish this in most areas.
The world of Silksong feels a lot more bright and lively (by design) while also being ruthless and punishing (sometimes overly so).
Mechanically this game feels awesome to play, the combat is as smooth as in HK while giving players a lot of tools to deal with everything the game throws at them. Silksong overall is harder than HKs basegame but also allows the player to approach the game in enough ways to make difficulty the players choice in the end.
The new areas are amazing, platformig is incredibly fun, the soundtrack is even better than the one of HK and the bosses are better than the bosses in HKs basegame by a really huge margin.
With all this said the game has some things (horrible currency economy, double contact damage, double environmental damage, bad runbacks) that are such obvious design errors which disincentivize exploration, experimentation and encourage/force mindless grinding. So while this game is an absolute blast and truly amazing it has some truly unecessary flaws and I still think the first HK (basegame + DLC everything included) is slightly better for it.
This game is a must play for fans of metroidvanias but I also very much recommend this game to players that are new to this genre and curious (though I think you should play the original HK first).

For my complaints, there’s that one boss runback, and the hidden walls feel even more ridiculous than in the first game. My biggest nitpick is probably the damage. Having regular enemies and bosses deal almost the same amount of damage makes the bosses feel less impactful. In the first game, I could really feel the danger and power of a boss when they hit me, especially the Dream bosses. I kinda miss that feeling in Silksong.

It’s a nitpick, but overall the game is really fun and I highly recommend it. I’d definitely recommend playing the first game before this one, but even without it, Silksong is still a great game.

I'm almost at 40 hours and have only scratched the surface. Everything from the music, art, and characters feel so intricately crafted. This time around, the focus is on saving a kingdom, rather than exploring one in ruin. It's a more hopeful journey with a sense of community, which is a welcome change of pace.

The combat is infamous for being challenging, but with how much customization you're provided, I feel that it balances out. You'll constantly find new items, abilities, and entirely new fighting styles that become unique to you. The gameplay will become addictive, and it has some of the best fights I've ever experienced in a game.
